target_customer: Mineral and royalty owners: funds, family offices, endowments, individuals and advisors
problem: Mineral owners cannot easily track revenue, wells, leases and documents across non-operated interests.
product_category: mineral and royalty portfolio management software

founders.name: Gabe Wilcox
founders.background_notes: Silicon Hills News says he comes from Arkansas and knows the mineral owner problem firsthand.

technical_complexity.rationale: Data aggregation and document management for oil and gas assets; the hard part was integrating revenue and well data.

defensibility.rationale: Customers store portfolios and documents in it, and a data partnership with Drillinginfo from 2017 added well data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Drillinginfo partnered in April 2017 and acquired MineralSoft in January 2019.

market_need_then: Drillinginfo's CEO described mineral ownership as a 1 trillion dollar asset class moving from a cottage industry (2019 quote). No 2016 demand data found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that was clear for the niche but gave no brand asset in sources.

outcome_analysis: MineralSoft came through YC Winter 2016, raised a 4 million Series A in February 2018 and partnered with Drillinginfo in 2017 before being acquired by it in January 2019 with about 35 staff. Price undisclosed. A founder with first-hand mineral owner experience and a niche with few focused tools likely helped, but sources do not give revenue or deal value.
notes: A search summary cites 9.2M raised to date (single aggregator, unverified). One aggregator claims Enverus bought it in 2018, which conflicts with the January 2019 deal. No dated 2016 competitor sources found; Royalty Advocate lists 2016 founding but is not dated coverage. The company's site mineralsoft.com was not fetched; the YC logo was a placeholder.
